This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Light review - LGTM

Clean refactor moving join_paths, get_checkpoint_run_config_filename, read_run_config, apply_run_config_backward_compat, and CONFIG_FILE into upstream megatron.training and re-exporting them from the bridge.

Verified:
- No stale references - call sites (auto_bridge.py, examples/peft/merge_lora.py, examples/conversion/adapter, tests) resolve via the bridge re-export or the new upstream import path.
- No dangling helpers - _sanitize_run_config_object, _RUNTIME_ONLY_TARGETS, _RECIPE_CONFIG_TARGET fully removed with no remaining references.
- No newly-unused imports - Path/sys/posixpath/lru_cache/MultiStorageClientFeature still used; yaml/logging/Any correctly dropped (no F401).
- No docs reference the moved symbols.

Two behavior-preservation items for a maintainer to confirm (this PR does not bump the MCore submodule):
1. Both conftest files call read_run_config.cache_clear(), which requires upstream to keep the lru_cache decorator on the moved function.
2. The old bridge read_run_config sanitized runtime-only targets (megatron.core.timers.Timers) and legacy RecipeConfig. The Timers test (test_read_run_config_sanitizes_runtime_only_targets) was deleted; RecipeConfig is still covered via test_quant_recipe_serialization.py, but no in-repo test now asserts Timers sanitization through the upstream function.

Suggested test cases
- No perf tests impacted.
- Confirm upstream coverage exists for the runtime-only-target (Timers) sanitization path previously verified by the removed test_read_run_config_sanitizes_runtime_only_targets.
- tests/unit_tests/training/utils/test_quant_recipe_serialization.py
- tests/unit_tests/training/utils/test_checkpoint_utils.py
- tests/unit_tests/training/test_checkpointing.py
- tests/unit_tests/models/gemma_vl/test_gemma3_vl_provider.py

two things with this file now:
1. Maybe we should keep all public functions that were exposed before still proxied at this file/import path, for anyone who was calling them directly?
2. There's some functions still duplicated like `join_paths()`, `get_run_config_filename()` , why not import those as well?
just want to confirm, in your opinion do existing MLM tests sufficiently cover the checkpoint utils, or do we need to migrate these?

1. I'd mention somewhere in documentation that we're consolidating train loops and ask to reuse imported functions from MLM. WDYT?
2. The problem is that we simplified `join_paths` in MLM and now some of MBridge unit tests are failing with that implemeentation. `get_run_config_filename` uses `join_paths` inside so had to keep these MBrige functions. But I have MLM PR which fixes it so we can remove these functions from MBridge once it's merged: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7741
good question. I'll take a look if we can move something from here to MLM
this PR adds few more unit tests: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7887
approved 7741, based on looking at some MSC docs. let's merge that first before this one.
1) also makes sense, can we do that in this PR?
